title: Brush Masters Painting vs. Precision Paint Experts
description: Comparing Brush Masters Painting and Precision Paint Experts? See why product names, coat counts, and back-brushing belong on every painting estimate.
h1: Brush Masters Painting vs. Precision Paint Experts
heroIntro: Two estimates can quote the same color and still describe very different finishes. This guide covers products, coat counts, and application methods.

questions: How many coats of paint should a painter apply?
Should a painting estimate name the paint product?

body: Brush Masters Painting is one of the painting and property-service companies homeowners in North Central Florida may be comparing. Whoever you call, the phrase "paint the house" leaves out the details that decide how long it lasts: which product, how many coats, and how it is applied. This guide is about getting those three things on paper from every bidder.

It is a fair request. A contractor who has priced your job already knows what it plans to use and how many passes it plans to make, so writing that down costs nothing. If an estimate stays vague after you ask, that tells you something too. The sections below explain what each detail means and why it changes the result on a Florida home.

"Premium paint" is not a product. Manufacturers sell several lines at very different price points, and the gap in durability is real. Ask each contractor to write down the manufacturer and product line for primer and topcoat on every surface.

Our estimates name the product. We work in premium Sherwin-Williams and Benjamin Moore lines and choose by surface: 100% acrylic on siding and trim, elastomeric on stucco with hairline movement, waterborne urethane enamel on cabinets, doors, and railings, and penetrating stains on exposed wood. Low-VOC options are available. Our guide to paint finishes explains sheen choices room by room.

sections.h2: Coat counts and how to check them
body: Two full coats is our baseline, with a third on dramatic color changes or porous surfaces. A single heavy coat might look fine on day one, but it rarely builds the film thickness a Florida exterior needs. When comparing bids, ask:
bullets: How many coats on walls, trim, and doors?
Is primer counted as a coat, or is it separate?
What happens if coverage is uneven after the stated coats?

body: Spraying is fast and can lay down an even film, but on rough or porous surfaces the paint may bridge over texture without working into it. Where penetration matters, our crews back-brush or back-roll sprayed surfaces while they are still wet. Ask any bidder how they handle this, especially on siding, stucco, and fences. You can read more on our exterior painting and trim and molding painting pages.

Once each estimate names the product, coat count, and method, comparison gets much easier. Ours comes free, usually within one business day of the walkthrough, and nothing is added later without your written approval. Request yours through our free quote page.

If you already have another bid in hand, hold on to it. Lay the two estimates side by side and compare product, coat count, and method surface by surface. Where they differ, ask both contractors to explain why. A good answer will reference the substrate and the exposure, not just the price, and it should hold up when you ask the same question twice.

faqs.q: Is Precision Paint Experts part of Brush Masters Painting?
faqs.a: No. We are a separate, locally owned company. This page is a buyer's guide to comparing estimates.

faqs.q: Do you always apply two coats?
faqs.a: Two full coats is our baseline. A third is added on dramatic color changes or porous surfaces, and the count is written into the estimate.

faqs.q: Which paint brands do you use?
faqs.a: Premium Sherwin-Williams and Benjamin Moore lines, chosen by surface, with the specific product named on your estimate.
